concepts.label: XDCR collection migration
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a third, distinct mapping mode alongside implicit and explicit mapping: migrating a subset of documents (selected by a regular expression, not a keyspace match) from a single, undifferentiated `_default` collection into a purpose-created target collection. Structurally different from explicit mapping - explicit mapping remaps keyspace names, migration filters and redistributes documents FROM one keyspace INTO several, based on document content rather than location. First contact anywhere in the corpus; genuinely UI-procedure-only, since neither the reference tree nor Capella's pages describe a data-redistribution workflow, only filtering and keyspace-to-keyspace mapping.

cross_component_finding: MIGRATION IS A THIRD MAPPING MODE THE REGISTRY'S EXISTING xdcr:replication-filter DESCRIPTION DOES NOT COVER. Round 20's xdcr:replication-filter concept describes filtering as restricting WHICH documents replicate; this page shows filtering additionally used to REDISTRIBUTE documents across multiple target collections based on content (city='San Francisco' -> California.SanFrancisco, then a second rule for SanJose, etc.), a data-modeling operation rather than a simple inclusion/exclusion gate. The CPU-intensiveness warning and the 2-simultaneous-migration-replication cap are both stated only here; no reference or Capella page discusses migration's performance cost at all.
